_readme: Single source for the demo video: narration, captions, on-screen texts, tx hashes and screenshot paths. Paths are relative to the repository root. Cue references: "c2" = start of cue 2 of the scene, "c2@0.5" = halfway through cue 2, "c2+0.4" = 0.4 s after its start, "end-2" = 2 s before the scene ends, a number = seconds after the scene starts. See demo/video/README.md.

meta.title: ReplayCourt - bug reports that prove themselves

cues.caption: Bug bounty programs are drowning in AI-written reports.
The Ethereum Foundation asks for up to a week. Cosmos reports 900 % more submissions. Decred paused its program.
cues.say: The Ethereum Foundation asks for up to a week. Cosmos reports nine hundred percent more submissions. Dee-cred paused its program.

cues.caption: And a valid Cosmos EVM report, marked “unable to reproduce”, was later exploited for $5.7M.

cues.caption: On chain: a commitment bound to the hunter, the sealed report, a bond.
The verifier replays it on an Ethereum fork, at the stated block.

cues.caption: NEAR gives escrow without a custodian, limited keys, an on-chain spending policy, and commit order that settles who was first.
Code and testnet logs are on GitHub.
Bounty teams: what would you need to see to trust a replay verdict?

tiles.title: Escrow without a custodian
tiles.text: Payouts, slashes and refunds follow the contract's rules. The contract owner cannot touch program funds.

tiles.title: Function-call access keys
tiles.text: The verifier and the AI hunter sign with keys that can call only their listed methods.

tiles.title: On-chain spending policy
tiles.text: The contract checks the vault's policy on every submission. Only a full-access key can change it.

tiles.title: On-chain commit order
tiles.text: Commit order is the submission id, so a valid earlier report wins a duplicate.
